content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The tumor is most likely the bright, hyperintense region on the image's left-posterior side (image right-lower), which spans roughly x 430–530 and y 350–530 in the left panel. In the right panel the same region is offset by about 784 px.

Marks near that region:
- 1000, at about (1254, 436), lies at the edge of the bright area.
- 1020, at about (1263, 489), lies in the bright area.
- 948, at about (1301, 422), lies near the dark structure on the right, which is probably a vessel or bone.
- 1042, at about (1268, 364), lies at the upper end of the bright area.

In the left panel, the bright mass runs from about (490, 360) down to (440, 490) and out to (520, 500). Subtracting 784 from the right-panel x values gives 1000 at x ≈ 470, y 436 and 1020 at x ≈ 479, y 489. Both fall within the bright region.

The bright area is widest and brightest around y 440–500, x 440–520. Mark 1020 at (479, 489) sits within this core. Mark 1000 at (470, 436) lies in a bright band that is slightly narrower. Mark 1020 is the better choice for the center.

ANSWER: 1020
